title: peer-contract v0.1 - Dispatch Routing
description: Core dispatch routing: explicit target_session_key, dispatch_id, dialog_key, source/target role. Solves core problem #1 (explicit routing) - prevents default-to-main and allows downstream rules (HR1, HR6) to validate routing intent.

dispatch_id.description: Unique ID for this dispatch. Generated by sender. Used for tracing, replay, AC chain references.

dialog_key.description: Logical dialog/conversation identifier. All dispatches in the same conversation share dialog_key. Used by recipient to thread context (without leaking session context across session boundaries - see isolation schema).

source_session_key.description: Sender session key. Must be a valid session key. Bus session keys MUST include a non-empty context-id segment (e.g. agent:<id>:bus:dashboard); bare agent:<id>:bus is rejected. Plugin/runtime uses this to infer sender_role (cross-checked against source_role claim).

target_session_key.description: Recipient session key. REQUIRED, no default. HR1 (no-default-to-main), HR5.1 (bus-context-required), and HR6 (session existence) enforced against this field. Bus session keys MUST include a non-empty context-id segment; bare agent:<id>:bus is rejected.

source_role.description: Sender's role. Should match inferred role from source_session_key. Plugin enforces this cross-check.

target_role.description: Recipient's role. HR2 (no cross-work direct) and HR3 (no user-to-work) enforced against this combination with source_role.

timestamp.description: ISO8601 dispatch creation time. Sender's clock. Used for ordering and TTL.

intent.description: Semantic intent. Drives bus flow selection (see 04-bus.schema.json).

in_reply_to.description: If this dispatch is a reply, points to the dispatch_id of the original. Forms the conversation tree.

parent_task_id.description: Day 8 v2 (2026-08-24, 老板 10:50 '结合 workboard'): Optional. If this dispatch depends on a prior task completing, set this to the **workboard card id** of the parent task. The peer-contract-enforcer plugin validates the UUID format (HR10 schema-only check). The actual dependency-graph enforcement (waiting for parent in 'done' status before child can be dispatched) is the workboard plugin's responsibility — wire up the edge via `workboard linkCards(parentCardId, childCardId)`. Use `workboard API createCard(...)` to make a card, get its id, then put that id here.

target_session_keys.description: Day 8 v2 (2026-08-24, 老板 10:50 '结合 workboard'): Optional. Multi-target fan-out (broadcast to N targets in a single dispatch). Mutually exclusive with `target_session_key` (use one or the other). Each entry must satisfy HR5.1 bus-context-required (bare `agent:<id>:bus` is rejected). Use this for 1-to-N broadcast; for 1-to-1 dispatch use `target_session_key`.

allOf.description: Cross-field invariants: HR1 + HR2 + HR3 + work-session restrictions

then.description: HR2: work session cannot dispatch directly to another work session - must go through bus
HR3: target=work requires explicit bus-relay path OR main-issued dispatch. Channel-originated → work blocked at runtime via messageProvider field.

allOf.description: HR1: target=main is only allowed for explicit non-routing intents (inform, query). task_assignment + main target = blocked.
Day 8 v2 (2026-08-24): target_session_key and target_session_keys are mutually exclusive. Use single (1:1) or array (1:N fan-out) but not both.
Day 8 v2 (2026-08-24): if target_session_keys is set, target_role MUST be 'bus' (multi-target fan-out only makes sense for bus coordination broadcasts).
